title: Streaming partial-JSON recovery and schema robustness tests
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Validate and harden the platform behavior when the API is asked to emit structured JSON under streaming and tool-calling flows. Specifically, exercise constrained-decoding enforcement and schema adherence when outputs are emitted incrementally, including partially-complete JSON tokens and deliberate edge cases produced by model variants. This ticket covers test harnesses, fuzz corpus generation, deterministic repair/rewind heuristics, and acceptance criteria for automatic fallback to non-streaming, tolerant-decoding, or schema-repair modes.

Why this matters: Customer apps rely on receiving valid JSON for function calls and downstream parsing. Streaming improves latency but increases the risk of partial/fragmented JSON. We need reproducible tests and recovery strategies so that canaries and rollouts don’t regress parsing reliability.

Scope:
- A matrix of tests across model families (open LLMs, tokenizers), sequence lengths, and chunking sizes.
- Constrained-decoding enabled vs disabled.
- Tool-calling flow where the model returns a JSON 'tool_call' payload mid-stream.
- Simulate network truncation, token corruption, and delayed final token.
- JS + Python client tests to ensure SDKs can recover, retry, or surface deterministic errors.

Out-of-scope: full production instrumentation dashboarding (separate follow-up), and on-prem installation packaging for Private (handled in dedicated ticket).
test_plan:
1) Create a fuzz corpus seeded from real customer prompts + synthetic edge cases (unclosed braces, stray commas, escaped unicode, multi-line strings).
2) Implement streaming harness that can pause/resume at arbitrary token boundaries and inject bitflip/delay behaviors.
3) Run constrained-decoding ON and OFF across corpus; capture partial outputs and final outputs.
4) Exercise tool-calling: require the model to emit a JSON tool call object mid-stream, then observe whether SDKs can buffer/assemble and validate schema.
5) Implement 'repair heuristics' module in harness: (a) try incremental re-parse, (b) attempt minimal bracket balancing, (c) escalate to non-streaming re-request with same prompt footprint.
6) Define metrics and failure classification (parse-fail, truncated, malformed-values, bad-types).
7) Automate nightly runs and add flaky detection to CI with sample seeds for regression tracing.
acceptance_criteria: Test harness can reproduce at least 95% of seeded failure classes deterministically across three runs
When constrained-decoding is enabled, rate of malformed JSON in final output decreases by >=70% relative to baseline for streaming runs
SDKs (JS/Python) implement deterministic buffering behavior: either deliver valid JSON or return a classified error with repair suggestion
Repair heuristics recover valid JSON for at least 40% of truncated-stream cases where the final token is missing
CI contains stable nightly job and failure seeds recorded in artifacts for debugging
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — identified three high-signal failure modes: mid-string truncation, escaped-quote miscounts, and trailing commas within nested arrays.
2026-03-04: Fuzz corpus implemented (seed size 1.2k prompts). Added random token-drop and chunk-reordering modes. Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/stream-json-fuzz (WIP).

2026-03-06: First harness run across gpt-style model variants with constrained-decoding ON: observed 62% reduction in malformed final JSON vs unconstrained baseline for short sequences, but only 28% for >1024 token sessions (investigating KV cache effects).
2026-03-08: Design review notes from PM @Rhea Singh: require SDK error codes to map to five canonical failure buckets and surfaced repair recommended action. Adding labels to test outputs.

2026-03-09: Eng review (PR #3482) added minimal-bracket-repair heuristic and 'resend-last-chunk' fallback. Benchmarked repair heuristic — recovers ~38% of truncated cases in our sample. Awaiting security sign-off for CI secrets to run on dedicated infra.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Repair heuristics could introduce silent data corruption if too aggressive. Mitigation: All repair attempts must produce provenance metadata (repair:method, original-bytes, patched-bytes) and be opt-in behind a runtime flag for 30-day A/B canary. If repair modifies values (not just structural brackets), fail-safe to non-streaming re-request is taken. Add verbose logging and telemetry with sample recording disabled by default for PII safety.
qa_notes: QA should run both constrained-decoding ON and OFF across: small (<=256 tokens), medium (512-1024), and long (>1024) sequences. Pay special attention to tool-calling tests where 'tool_call' appears before EOS; validate SDK behavior when streams include multiple tool calls. Record seeds for any flaky cases and add to exclusion list after triage.
